title: システム思考
subtitle: Systems Thinking
keywords: System Design 2.Stok, Flow, Feed-back loop 3.Resilience, Hierarchy, Self organization 4.Levalage
educationalGoal: This course is for an educational goal of the Dept. of Management Systems to acquire "Information design basic ability". The environment surrounding us is composed of various things intricately intertwined. Even if systems are observed and analyzed from only one aspect and modeled or made into IT, not only the expected effect may not be obtained, but also new problems may be created. Students will learn not only static modeling, but also components behavior and feedback that change over time.
advice: The events occurring in the world are composed of various things and their relationships intricately intertwined. Students will learn methods to model and analyze dynamically changing structures and relationships, as well as changes and stability of the entire system. First, students will acquire the basic skills to read and understand the data accurately, and perform initial analysis based on practical tasks. Next, students will learn about the stock, flow, and feedback loop as the basic structure and behavior of the system. Then students will learn resilience, self-organization, hierarchy as a function of the system, and concrete the ability to search for intervention places as leverage points.
books: Thinking in Systems: A Primer, Donella H. Meadows, Chelsea Green Pub Co; Illusrated version (2008/12/3), ISBN: 978-1603580557 (Kindle version is also available) Factfulness Illustrated, Hans Rosling, et. al., Sceptre (2019/10/3) ISBN: 978-1473637467
requiredKnowledge: To take and earn credits for "System Modeling," which is a second-year class in the Department of Management Information is essential. It is not necessary to take other courses for basic information design skills up to the 1st semester of junior, but it is desirable that you have already taken them. It is also recommended that you will take "Advanced Programming Applications" at the same time.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand and explain the basics of systems thinking.
Be able to explain the basic roles of stock, flow, dynamics, feedback.
Be able to explain system constraints, disturbance recovery, self-organization, and the trade-offs.
Be able to use a modeler to model complicated systems.
Be able to acquire basic skills to read and understand data accurately.
